evidence: Migration 0128_patient_access_pin_notice_and_named_requester.sql. WHAT IT DOES: (1) notification.on_identity_pin_outbox_created() and the trigger pin_use_notification_inbox, AFTER INSERT on identity.outbox_events WHEN event_type = 'PatientAccessPinVerified', place one PATIENT_ACCESS_PIN_USED item (resource consent-grant, the grant id) in the patient's in-app inbox through 0037's notification.enqueue_patient_inbox_item, with metadata consentGrantId, reviewRequired true, and, read from the grant the PIN created, its scope, the clinician's staff name (identity.staff.full_name), their membership role at the facility and the facility's name (a snapshot at the moment of use; values that cannot be read are left out). A PIN replay, a wrong PIN or a lock-out writes no outbox event (0098, 0122, 0123), so no item; a patient without an active account gets none (the enqueue's rule); a break-glass grant keeps 0037's own notice only. The outbox event, its payload rule and the EventBridge rule are unchanged. (2) identity.list_my_access_requests() gains requester_name and requester_role (columns 13 and 14: the request's staff name and its membership's role at the request's facility, null when unknown); dropped and recreated with 0104's owner and EXECUTE for hid_identity_runtime only (runtime-grants.sql unchanged). identity-api adds requesterName and requesterRole when the columns exist; an older image ignores them. NOT PORTED: main 0091 sections 1-3 and the access history's named grantee and truncated flag. SAFETY: SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp; the notice function is owned like 0037's emergency notice, revoked from PUBLIC and granted to no role; md5 pins of the enqueue, the emergency notice and 0104's list; the PIN payload rule naming the scope (0122) and 0123's QA marker as preconditions.
